question.worked_solution:
The $3$rd row of the matrix contains two zeros, more than any other row. So using a Laplace expansion along the $3$rd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}| & =1\cdot {C}_{31}+2\cdot {C}_{32}+0\cdot {C}_{33}+0\cdot {C}_{34} \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{3+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 2 \\ -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}|+2\cdot (-1)^{3+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 2 \\ -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}|-2|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the first $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $3$rd row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 2 \\ -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}| & =1\cdot {C}_{31}+0\cdot {C}_{32}+5\cdot {C}_{33} \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{3+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}|+5\cdot (-1)^{3+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}|+5|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =(1-4)+5(6-3) \\  & =-3+15 \\  & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the second $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{21}+2\cdot {C}_{22}+(-1)\cdot {C}_{23} \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{2+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}|+(-1)\cdot (-1)^{2+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(5+4)+(0-2) \\  & =18-2 \\  & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}|=1\cdot 12-2\cdot 16=-20.
$$
